chapter: Marriages, Tong Funeral and Liberation Music
title: Playing piano and organ on A Genuine Tong Funeral
summary: Shown the personnel, she says she played composer's piano and organ and other parts as needed but was not a serious pianist then.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Can I go back to A Genuine Tong Funeral and the one thing I want to address here, makes me think that your, not just your composing life was continuing to grow and expand, but as a pianist was starting to become part of the factor there too. Because you’re listed on here in the personnel, as... and maybe you’re listed as... Well, it’s Gary Burton, Vibraphone, Carla Bley, piano, organ, and conductor.
I had no idea I played piano and organ on those... that album. I guess I did!
I was not... no. It was just composer’s piano.
Ok. So this is the... the record is incorrect. And the rest of the band was kind of interesting too. It lists Larry Coryell of course, Steve Lacy, soprano saxophone, Gato Bobbieri?
Yeah. Those were the guys that I liked at the time.
This is wonderful. Jimmy Knepper, uhh, Michael Mantler, Howard Johnson, Steve Swallow, and of course Bob.
It isn’t that that’s incorrect, your information. It’s just that I played piano and organ on that probably and I probably also played chains and glockenspiel and anything else that was necessary.
But I wasn’t a serious piano player. I didn’t practice.
So it was what your composition called for but it was more, it was more... it was written out or orchestrated in a way that those were the parts that you’re playing.

I don’t think I played on everything. I might have played on a couple of tunes, I don’t know. I haven’t heard it in a long time. But basically if in the piece there was a piano part I played it if there was no one else there.
